title: Kaziranga National Park
text: UNESCO World Heritage site and home to the largest population of the Indian one-horned rhinoceros, plus tigers, wild water buffalo, swamp deer and many birds. Jeep safaris run in the Central (Kohora), Western, Eastern and Burapahar ranges; elephant-back rides are limited. The park is closed during the monsoon flooding and usually reopens around 1 November (some years mid-October). About 4-5 hours by road from Guwahati.

title: Majuli River Island
text: One of the world's largest inhabited river islands in the Brahmaputra, centre of Assamese neo-Vaishnavite culture with satras (monasteries), mask-making at Samaguri, pottery and Mishing tribal villages. Reached by ferry from Nimati Ghat near Jorhat (about 1.5 hours). Plan at least 1 night. Erosion and floods affect the island; ferry times change with water level.

title: Manas National Park
text: UNESCO World Heritage site and tiger reserve on the Bhutan border with golden langur, pygmy hog, elephants and rare birds. Jungle safaris and river rafting on the Manas river. Quieter than Kaziranga. Best visited in the dry months.

title: Sivasagar and Ahom monuments
text: Capital region of the 600-year Ahom kingdom: Rang Ghar (two-storey royal pavilion), Talatal Ghar, Sivasagar Tank and the Charaideo mound-burials (maidams). A good cultural stop between Kaziranga and Dibrugarh tea country.

title: Assam tea estate stays
text: Heritage tea-planter bungalows around Jorhat and Dibrugarh offer estate walks, factory visits and tea tasting. Peak plucking is roughly Apr-Nov. A relaxed add-on after wildlife and culture stops.

title: Shillong
text: Hill-station capital of Meghalaya, about 100 km (3 hours) from Guwahati. Umiam Lake, Don Bosco Museum of indigenous cultures, Elephant Falls, Laitlum Canyons and the Police Bazaar food streets. Good base for Cherrapunji and Mawlynnong day trips.

title: Cherrapunji (Sohra)
text: One of the wettest places on Earth. Nohkalikai Falls, Seven Sisters Falls, Mawsmai Cave and the double-decker living root bridge near Nongriat (about 3,500 steps down - wear good shoes). Monsoon (Jun-Sep) brings heavy rain, fog and landslide risk; clearer views Oct-Apr.

title: Mawsmai Cave
text: Well-lit limestone cave near Cherrapunji, about 150 m of walkable passage, takes roughly 30-45 minutes. Narrow squeezes in places. Often combined with Nohkalikai Falls in a half-day.

title: Dawki and Mawlynnong
text: Dawki on the Umngot river is known for very clear water and boat rides at the Bangladesh border; Mawlynnong is a tidy Khasi village with a living root bridge nearby. Roughly 3-4 hours from Shillong. Best in the dry, clear season (Nov-Apr).

title: Tawang
text: Home of Tawang Monastery, among the largest Buddhist monasteries in India, at about 3,000 m altitude. Route crosses Sela Pass (about 4,170 m) which can close with snow in winter. Altitude sickness is possible - acclimatise. Needs an Inner Line Permit for Indian non-residents. Roughly 2 days by road from Guwahati/Tezpur.

title: Ziro Valley
text: Rice-field valley home to the Apatani tribe, pine forests and village walks. Hosts the Ziro Music Festival (usually September). Needs an Inner Line Permit for Indian non-residents. Several hours from Itanagar/Naharlagun by road.

title: Namdapha National Park
text: Large, remote tiger reserve in the eastern Himalaya with rich rainforest wildlife and rare big-cat diversity. Basic lodging, long road transfers from Miao, limited facilities - for committed nature travellers. Permits required.

title: Kohima
text: Hill capital of Nagaland: the WWII Kohima War Cemetery and Naga Heritage Village at Kisama, site of the Hornbill Festival (1-10 December). Nearest rail/air hub is Dimapur, about 2.5 hours away. Inner Line Permit needed for Indian non-residents.

title: Dzukou Valley
text: Day or overnight trek to a high valley of rolling grassland, famous for lilies and flowers in summer (about Jun-Sep). Starts from Viswema or Zakhama near Kohima. Weather turns fast; carry layers.

title: Khonoma village
text: Angami Naga 'green village' with terraced fields, stone-gate heritage and community conservation of forest. Easy half-day from Kohima. Homestays available.

title: Loktak Lake
text: Largest freshwater lake in the Northeast with floating 'phumdis' and the floating Keibul Lamjao National Park, last home of the sangai (brow-antlered deer). Boat rides and sunsets from Sendra. About 1.5 hours from Imphal. Inner Line Permit rules apply for Indian non-residents.

title: Imphal
text: Kangla Fort, Ima Keithel (the all-women market), Manipur State Museum and INA memorial at Moirang. Airport connects to Guwahati and Kolkata. Check current permit and security advisories before travel.

title: Ukhrul and Shirui
text: Tangkhul Naga hill district known for the Shirui Lily, flowering around May with a lily festival. Remote; arrange transport and permits in advance and check advisories.

title: Aizawl
text: Ridge-top capital with cafes, Mizoram State Museum and Bara Bazar. Fly into Lengpui airport (about 35 km) or drive from Silchar. Inner Line Permit needed for Indian non-residents.

title: Champhai and Murlen
text: Border town with rice-bowl valley, Rih Dil lake across the border and Murlen National Park for birding and hill walks. Long road from Aizawl (about 6 hours).

title: Reiek Tlang
text: Hill with village-style viewpoints and a short trek about 30 km from Aizawl; easy half-day with sunset views.

title: Agartala
text: Ujjayanta Palace (state museum), Tripura Sundari Temple at Udaipur and Sepahijala wildlife sanctuary. Airport and rail link to the mainland. No Inner Line Permit for Indian nationals at the time of drafting.

title: Neermahal
text: Water palace in Rudrasagar Lake built by the Tripura king in the early 20th century. Boat access; best seen in the dry season when water is calm.

title: Unakoti rock carvings
text: Huge rock-cut Shaiva carvings in a forest ravine, about 180 km from Agartala. Ashokashtami Mela is held in spring. A full day trip or overnight.

title: Gangtok
text: Capital with MG Marg pedestrian street, Rumtek Monastery and ropeway views. Reach via Bagdogra airport/NJP railway, about 4-5 hours by road. Base for Tsomgo Lake and Nathu La, which need permits.

title: Tsomgo Lake and Nathu La
text: High-altitude glacial lake (about 3,750 m) and the Indo-China border pass Nathu La (about 4,300 m). Permits are arranged through registered travel agents and are subject to quotas and closures; Nathu La is often closed on certain weekdays and in bad weather. Altitude sickness possible.

title: Pelling
text: Quiet hill town with Kanchenjunga views, Pemayangtse Monastery and the Rabdentse ruins. Clear mornings in autumn and spring.

title: Yumthang Valley
text: Alpine valley famous for rhododendron bloom roughly Apr-May. North Sikkim requires permits; landslides can cut the road in monsoon. Gurudongmar Lake (about 5,400 m) further north needs an early start and acclimatisation.

title: Permits overview for the Northeast
text: As of drafting: Assam, Meghalaya and Tripura generally do not need an Inner Line Permit (ILP) for Indian nationals. Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Mizoram and Manipur require an ILP for Indian non-residents, obtained online or on arrival at designated points. Sikkim needs special permits for areas like Nathu La, Tsomgo and North Sikkim. Foreign nationals need Protected/Restricted Area Permits in several states. Rules change often - always check the official state portal.

title: Arunachal Pradesh permits
text: Indian non-residents need an Inner Line Permit (ILP), applied for through the state e-ILP portal or at entry checkpoints. Foreign nationals need a Protected Area Permit, usually via a registered tour operator. Carry printed copies and ID for checkposts. Verify current rules with the state government.

title: Nagaland permits
text: Indian non-residents need an Inner Line Permit; Dimapur and Kohima have facilitation counters and an online process exists. Foreign nationals follow restricted-area rules and register with local police. Check current rules before travel.

title: Manipur permits and advisories
text: Indian non-residents need an Inner Line Permit to enter Manipur. Security and curfew conditions have varied; check current travel advisories and local news before planning.

title: Mizoram permits
text: Indian non-residents need an Inner Line Permit, available online or at entry points such as Lengpui airport and Vairengte. Foreigners must register with local authorities. Verify current rules.

title: Sikkim permits
text: Nathu La, Tsomgo (Changu) Lake, North Sikkim (Yumthang, Lachung, Gurudongmar) and some border areas need permits arranged through registered agents in Gangtok. Carry ID photos and copies. Quotas and weather closures apply. Verify before travel.

title: Assam, Meghalaya and Tripura permits
text: Indian nationals generally need no Inner Line Permit for Assam, Meghalaya or Tripura at the time of drafting. Some protected-area entries (national parks) need an entry ticket and safari booking. Carry government photo ID. Verify if rules change.

title: Best time to visit by region
text: Broadly Oct-Apr is the main season for Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura. Monsoon (Jun-Sep) brings heavy rain, floods and landslides, especially Assam, Meghalaya and Arunachal; Kaziranga is closed then. Sikkim and Arunachal are good Mar-May and Oct-Nov, with high-altitude road closures in deep winter. Hornbill Festival in Nagaland is 1-10 December.

title: Getting there: main gateways
text: Guwahati (LGBI airport and rail) is the main gateway for Assam, Meghalaya and onward Arunachal. Bagdogra/Siliguri serves Sikkim and Darjeeling. Dimapur serves Nagaland, Imphal airport serves Manipur, Lengpui serves Aizawl, and Agartala has its own airport and rail. Shillong is about 3 hours from Guwahati; Kaziranga about 4-5 hours; Tawang about 2 days by road.

title: Sample 7-day Assam + Meghalaya
text: Day 1 Guwahati and Kamakhya; Days 2-3 Kaziranga safaris; Day 4 Majuli or travel via Jorhat; Days 5-6 Shillong, Cherrapunji, Mawsmai Cave and living root bridges; Day 7 Dawki or Laitlum then back to Guwahati. Blend of wildlife, culture and nature.

title: Sample 8-day Sikkim
text: Day 1 Bagdogra to Gangtok; Day 2 Gangtok sights and Rumtek; Day 3 Tsomgo Lake and Nathu La (permit); Days 4-5 Pelling, Pemayangtse and Rabdentse; Days 6-7 North Sikkim if permits and weather allow; Day 8 back to Bagdogra.

title: Sample 10-day Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland
text: Guwahati and Kaziranga (3 days), Shillong and Cherrapunji (3 days), then Dimapur to Kohima and Khonoma (3 days) with the Hornbill Festival in early December if dates match, return via Dimapur.
